strategies.name: Baseline Sequential All-Reduce Chain
strategies.desc: Executes 8 sequential all-reduce operations with intermediate local bidiagonal coupling and uncoupling transformations. Total 8 all-reduce dispatches handling full W*S=229376 elements each. Represents the straightforward approach with no fusion or overlap, maximizing simplicity at the cost of serialized communication latency.

strategies.name: Reduce-Scatter + All-Gather Decomposition
strategies.desc: Replaces each all-reduce with a reduce-scatter followed by all-gather pair, allowing each rank to compute its local shard's coupling independently during the all-gather phase. Results in 16 collective dispatches (8 RS + 8 AG) but with smaller per-dispatch payloads (W*S/W = 1024 elements for RS). Trades dispatch count for reduced per-operation bandwidth and potential for better pipelining.

strategies.name: Fused Bidiagonal Transform with Buffering
strategies.desc: Pre-allocates intermediate buffers and fuses the forward coupling, all-reduce, and backward uncoupling into combined kernel launches before each collective. Uses 8 all-reduce dispatches on full tensors but amortizes local computation overhead through vectorized operations on contiguous memory. Optimizes for minimal dispatch count while hiding local transformation costs.

strategies.name: Hierarchical Two-Level Reduction
strategies.desc: Exploits potential node/device hierarchy by performing intra-node reductions (assuming multi-node topology) followed by inter-node all-reduce, then broadcasting back. For 224 ranks this could structure as 28 nodes × 8 devices, using 8×(intra-reduce + inter-all-reduce + broadcast) = 24 collective dispatches but with dramatically smaller inter-node payloads. Balances bandwidth usage across network tiers.

strategies.name: Pipelined Chunk-Based All-Reduce
strategies.desc:
Splits the W*S tensor into multiple chunks and pipelines all-reduce operations across stages, allowing overlap between computation (bidiagonal coupling) on one chunk while communicating another. Requires 8×C collective dispatches where C is chunk count (e.g., C=4 yields 32 dispatches) with chunk size W*S/C. Optimizes for latency hiding through computation-communication overlap at the cost of increased dispatch overhead.
